title: Condo board members among five victims in Vaughan shooting, police say
article: Police say three of the five people killed in a shooting at a Vaughan condo tower were members of the condo board.
Three men and two women were shot in three seperate units on different floors, according to York Regional Police.
The suspected gunman in Sunday's massacre - 73-year-old Francesco Villi - lived in the building on Jane St. just north of Rutherford Rd., along with the victims he allegedly targeted.
The victims who were fatally shot had not been identified as of late Monday afternoon.
A 66-year-old woman, identified by the Amalgamated Transit Union as Doreen Di Nino, was shot and was undergoing emergency surgury in hospital on Monday.

"This is obviously a very difficult time for my family and I would ask that our privacy be respected," said John Di Nino, President, ATU Canada, who is married to Doreen and is a member of the condo board apparently targeted.
Investigators and forensics experts were on the scene throughout Monday.

"We realize a crime of this magnitude is traumatizing for friends and family who at this time of year, especially now, must deal with the tragic death of their loved ones." said York Regional Police Chief Jim MacSween.
"The motive for the shooting remains part of this very complicated and very fluid investigation, which is still ongoing at this time," he added.
Officers arrived three minutes after the first call about a man with a gun at 7:21 p.m.
The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) said the suspect was armed with a semi-automatic handgun.
Villi was killed in an interaction with an officer on the third floor, the SIU said.

"I don't believe there was an exchange of gunfire. There was a number of shots from one officer. A number of those shots struck the man and he was pronounced deceased at the scene," said SIU spokesperson Kristy Denette.
Several people placed flowers outside the building on Monday as residents described the frightening scene the night before.
"It's very scary. Especially what happened to me. I was coming down the stairs and all the police were coming up the stairs - all with their guns," said Matteo Sivitilli, who lives on the 11th floor.
"They pointed to me and said, 'stop, stop.' I stopped and said, 'I live upstairs. What do you want?' Then they searched me."

Sivitilli said he knew of years of conflict between Villi and the condo board. Court documents indicate a man with the same name as the alleged gunman had a long-standing dispute with his condo board.
"I knew him," said. "I was talking to him all the time. He was telling me all of his complaints. And he wasn't feeling good. He (said he) used to get some fumes from under his unit."
In a court ruling Aug. 4, Justice Di Luca rejected Villi's claim of more than $8,000,000 against the condo board.

"Mr. Villi believes that the electrical room which sits beneath his unit is improperly constructed, resulting in the emission of electromagnetic waves which have caused him significant pain and suffering over the years," the judge wrote.
"I conclude that the statement of claim is, on its face, fatally flawed. It is plain and obvious that it cannot succeed and therefore must be struck."

Court documents also show the board sought a restraining order in 2018 against Villi for his "allegedly threatening, abusive, intimidating and harassing behaviour" towards the board, property management, workers and residents.
Police said they could not comment on whether the suspected gunman was a registered firearms owner.
